lead: Virginia Beach plumbing deals with a high water table, coastal flooding, salt air and homes from the 1970s to 1990s boom. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Virginia Beach.
risk: polybutylene pipe, flooding and backups, and water heater replacement
risk_short: old pipes, flooding and water heaters
why: Virginia Beach grew fast from the 1970s through the 1990s, so many homes are 30 to 50 years old. Homes from the late 1970s to the mid-1990s may have gray polybutylene pipe.
Low ground and a high water table mean nor'easters and hurricanes flood streets and back up drains. Many homes sit on slabs or crawl spaces close to the water table.
water: Virginia Beach buys treated water from Norfolk, which draws from local reservoirs and from Lake Gaston by pipeline. The water is moderately soft.
tips: Look for gray pipe stamped PB2110.
Shut off the main valve before an evacuation.
Check crawl-space drainage after big storms.
areas: PipeMend works at the Oceanfront and in Great Neck, Kempsville, Chic's Beach, Sandbridge, Princess Anne, Lynnhaven and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Virginia Beach Permits and Inspections Division, and plumbers must hold a tradesman license from the Virginia Board for Contractors (DPOR).

faq.q: Are polybutylene pipes common in Virginia Beach?
faq.a: They show up in many homes built from the late 1970s to the mid-1990s, when the city grew fast. Look for gray plastic pipe stamped PB2110. Replacing it before it fails avoids water damage.
